s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic autoimmune disorder with sicca symptoms, Raynaud phenomenon, and calcinosis
salient_findings: 20-year history of oral and ocular sicca symptoms
Asymptomatic elevation of creatinine kinase levels
Painless pinpoint white nodules in the subcutaneous plane of the right fifth finger
Soft-tissue calcifications in the distal first and fifth fingers
key_facts: 56-year-old woman
History of hypothyroidism and hyperlipidemia
20-year history of oral and ocular sicca symptoms
Asymptomatic elevation of creatinine kinase levels
Negative myositis and muscular dystrophy panel
Negative muscle biopsy results
Chronic stable autoimmune thrombocytopenia
Previous medications included methotrexate and low-dose steroids
Currently on hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily
Does not take calcium or vitamin D supplements
Mild dryness of mouth and throat
Raynaud phenomenon
Painless pinpoint white nodules in the subcutaneous plane of the right fifth finger
Soft-tissue calcifications in the distal first and fifth fingers
Positive for antinuclear antibody 1:160 titer, nucleolar pattern, and anti-Ro
Biopsy of digit lesions from right thumb and fourth finger consistent with calcinosis

shortlist.label: CREST syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including Raynaud phenomenon, calcinosis, and esophageal reflux are not mentioned but the presence of Raynaud phenomenon and calcinosis are key features of CREST syndrome. The patient also has a positive antinuclear antibody and anti-Ro, which are common in autoimmune diseases. The combination of these features makes CREST syndrome the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Limited systemic scleroderma
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of limited systemic scleroderma, such as Raynaud phenomenon and calcinosis, the absence of skin tightening and other features makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's oral and ocular sicca symptoms are consistent with Sjögren's syndrome, but the presence of calcinosis and Raynaud phenomenon suggests a more complex autoimmune disease.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The patient's combination of autoimmune features, including positive antinuclear antibody and anti-Ro, could suggest mixed connective tissue disease, but the specific features of CREST syndrome are more prominent.

rejected.label: Calcinosis cutis
rejected.why: While the patient has calcinosis, this is a feature of CREST syndrome, and the diagnosis of calcinosis cutis alone does not account for the patient's other symptoms.
